newsitem.title: USA: Maxus Energy boosts exploration budget.
newsitem.headline: Maxus Energy boosts exploration budget.

text.p: Maxus Energy Corp, the U.S. unit of YPF SA, budgeted $352 million for capital spending in 1997, up from $269 million last year, president Roberto Monti said on Friday.
After a year spent paring costs and returning the company to profitability, Maxus plans to step up exploration in its core areas, Monti told Reuters after a speech to a Houston business group.
"Venezuela is going to be one of our focal points. That is normal, that is what we like to do, we like to grow in the Americas," he said.

The Dallas-based company owns rights with British Petroleum Co Plc and Amoco Corp to the Guarapiche block in Venezuela, where the partners plan to conduct three-dimensional seismic studies to identify potential drilling sites, he said.

Monti said Maxus may eventually abandon exploration in Africa if it fails to tap into commercial reserves in Tunisia and Algeria. "Everything will depend on the success of the exploration. If we succeed, we will stay, and if we don't succeed, we will pack up and come home," he said.
